thread:
Evan: quick q — for the new A/B rollout we've been seeing oscillations when fallback triggers. should we pick a single global 'anchor' (stable variant) or allow per-tenant anchors? observability shows noisy latencies when traffic is split
Priya: I'd lean per-tenant anchors to reduce cross-tenant noise. downside: more state and edge cases for tenants with little history. can we hybrid it?
Marta: hybrid sounds practical — per-tenant anchor when we have >= N requests in the lookback, otherwise fall back to a global anchor. global anchor is the release prior to canary.
Ben: operational tradeoffs: per-tenant needs lookups, TTLs, and storing warm caches (KV cost). also affects routing decisions on the proxy. worth measuring cost vs latency improvement.
Priya: on telemetry: propose a composite "regression score" made from p95 latency delta (normalized), new error-rate, and a lightweight quality signal (eval prompt regression or sanity checks). require min sample size (e.g., samples >= 250) before acting.
Evan: what statistical test? i'm worried about noisy signals causing false positives (type I). frequentist t-tests are brittle here.
Marta: suggest a Bayesian approach (posterior probability that canary worse than anchor by margin delta) + deterministic circuit-breaker on absolute thresholds (e.g., error-rate > 1.5% or p95 latency > 300ms). both must hold.
observability-bot: ALERT: p95 increased 22% for canary/model-v2 in us-west-2 hostpool. see https://obs.local/d/abcd1234/canary-v2?orgId=1 : samples=120
Ben: that sample size is below the minimum — we should avoid auto-fallback for now, but surface a high-priority alert to oncall.
Priya: here's a quick pseudocode for the score calc i had in mind:
```python
# normalized inputs in [0,1]
score = 0.6 * latency_delta_norm + 0.3 * error_rate_norm + 0.1 * quality_regression_norm
if samples >= 250 and posterior_prob(canary_worse) > 0.95 and score > 0.7:
    trigger_fallback(target=anchor_priority_list)
```
Evan: ok. anchor_priority_list = [tenant_pinned, tenant_previous_release, global_previous_release, safe_stub]. fallback action should be deterministic and idempotent. also prefer graceful drain: scale traffic down over 5 minutes with immediate circuit for severe errors.
Marta: and we should record the fallback reason as structured metadata (reason_code, metric_snapshot, sample_count) so Optimize/Console can show root cause.
Ben: implementation notes — per-tenant anchors require a small kv table: key=(tenant,model_family)->anchor_version + last_seen_ts + sample_count. keep TTL 7d, fallback to global if missing. we can shard the table by tenant-hash.
Priya: optics: add a small canary-sim harness to the test infra to simulate noisy latencies and verify thresholds. i'll take that on after we lock thresholds.
Evan: perfect. @Priya can you sanity-check the weights/thresholds tomorrow? @Marta please start an RFC draft with these pieces: telemetry signals, sample thresholds, anchor TTL semantics, fallback priority, and rollback/drain choreography.
Marta: will do. i'll put a sketch in docs and link it to a follow-up design review.
Evan: thanks all. short-term: ops, set oncall runbook to not auto-fallback unless samples>=250. we'll iterate after the sim results.
